items.title: Email Campaign · . Referral Push (30-60 Day Post-Install, Satisfied Clients)
items.preview:
**Why this is #1:** These are your freshest, happiest customers (30-60 days in, before any friction). This window has the highest referral intent. Direct cash incentive, warm audience, and a clear single CTA. Highest expected conversion of anything available this week.
### 1. Campaign + Audience
- **Campaign name:** "The Neighbor Question". Referral Push
- **Audience size:** 30 contacts (30-60 day post-install, satisfied)
### 2. Subject Lines (60 char max)
- **Primary:** Your neighbors keep asking about your water
- **Alt 1 (curiosity):** Quick question about your new water
- **Alt 2 (specific):** $500 when a neighbor loves their water too
- **Alt 3 (pain):** The water complaint every neighbor shares
- **Alt 4 (authority):** Most of our best clients came from one thing
### 3. Preview Text (90 char max)
Noticed the difference yet? There's a thank-you in it when you share it.
### 4. Email Body
> Hi Anna,
>
> It's been a few weeks now, and by this point most folks start to notice the little things. Cleaner glassware. Softer skin after a shower. Water that just tastes the way it should.
>
> Here's the thing: the best compliment you can give us is a name.
>
> When you refer a neighbor, friend, or family member and they book a free water assessment, you get a $50 gift card just for the introduction. If they move forward and become a client, you get $500 cash. And it scales from there: $750 once you've sent us six, $1,000 once you hit ten in a year.
>
> No pressure, no catch. Just reply to this email with a name, or forward it along and tell them to mention you.
>
> Thanks for trusting us with your home's water.
>
>. Justin
> CEO / ClearWave
*(Note: Anna's system field is "Meridian + RO + Upgraded faucet". MERIDIAN is a current brand name, so it could be named. I kept it generic here since the referral angle doesn't need the product reference. If you want it personalized, add: "Your MERIDIAN setup has been dialed in for a few weeks now.")*
### 5. Send Timing
**Tuesday, 10:00 AM ET**. Mid-morning Tuesday is a reliable B2C open window; avoids Monday inbox clutter.
### 6. Expected Performance
- **Open:** 48-55% (above your 42.3% baseline. Small, warm, recently-engaged list with a personal subject line)
- **Click/reply:** 4-8% (referral asks with cash incentives and a reply-based CTA outperform your 0.28% click avg dramatically, because the action is "reply," not "click")
- **Conversion (names submitted):** 2-4 referrals realistically; even 1 closed referral returns $500 against near-zero send cost
### 7. Source Justification
- **Hard Rule 3** (push referrals, never reviews) + **Rule 3a** ("free water assessment" exact phrase)
- **Referral Bonus Structure** (exact $50 / $500 / $750 / $1,000 tiers)
- Jobber trigger: "Referral push candidates (30-60 days post-install, satisfied): 30"

items.title: Email Campaign · . Concierge "Is It Worth It?" (13-24 Month Clients)
items.preview:
**Why this is #2:** 100 candidates, all past their year-1 service (so they trust the service experience), none currently on Concierge. The "here's the math" framing converts recurring revenue without feeling pushy. Larger list = more absolute conversions even at a modest rate.
### 1. Campaign + Audience
- **Campaign name:** "The Year 1.5 Question". Concierge Upsell
- **Audience size:** 100 contacts (13-24 months post-install, not on Concierge)
### 2. Subject Lines (60 char max)
- **Primary:** The question we get asked at month 18
- **Alt 1 (curiosity):** Is Concierge actually worth it for you?
- **Alt 2 (specific):** Here's the Concierge math, honestly
- **Alt 3 (authority):** What your annual service really covers
- **Alt 4 (pain):** Tired of tracking your own filter swaps?
### 3. Preview Text (90 char max)
No pressure. Just the honest math on whether Concierge makes sense for your home.
### 4. Email Body
> Hi Cory,
>
> It's been about 20 months since we installed your water system, which means you've been through at least one annual service with us by now. Thank you for that.
>
> Here's the question we get asked around this point: "Is this Concierge thing actually worth it for me?" Fair question. Here's the honest math.
>
> Concierge is $99/mo. It covers your annual service, all filter swaps, priority phone support, and parts coverage on your standard install components. If you're currently handling service pay-as-you-go or tracking filter changes yourself, it usually comes out ahead once you add up a service visit plus filters plus the occasional part.
>
> The bigger value for most folks: you stop thinking about it. We track the schedule, we show up, your water stays the way it should.
>
> If that sounds worth a look, just reply and I'll have the team walk you through whether it pencils out for your specific setup. If not, no worries at all.
>
>. Justin
> CEO / ClearWave
*(Note: Cory's system field is "NeuMAX + H2O Protector + Sediment Filter". All legacy/forbidden names, so I used the blanket tenure line per Rule 2: "It's been about 20 months since we installed your water system." Install date 2025-07-17 to now ≈ 20 months. Merge logic should compute [X months] per contact.)*
### 5. Send Timing
**Thursday, 11:00 AM ET**. Later in the week for a considered, financial-decision read; midday when people have headspace.
### 6. Expected Performance
- **Open:** 40-46% (near baseline; "the math" / "worth it" subject lines suit a trusting, serviced audience)
- **Click/reply:** 2-5% (reply-based soft CTA; your recurring clients already trust the service experience)
- **Conversion:** 3-7 new Concierge sign-ups realistic. At $99/mo, even 5 conversions = ~$5,940/yr recurring from one email
### 7. Source Justification
- **Concierge Upsell Context** (exact $99/mo scope, "is this worth it / here's the math" framing, not-pushy voice)
- **Hard Rule 1** (never before 12 months. List is pre-filtered to 13-24 months, compliant)
- **Hard Rule 2** (legacy names suppressed via tenure line; no translation attempted)
- Jobber trigger: "Concierge upsell candidates (13-24 months, NOT on Concierge): 100"
---
## Why NOT the cold list this week
The 1,000 cold subscribers are tempting on volume, but your recent broadcast-style campaigns ("Your Discount Ends Today," "Water Minute") cratered at 0.4-0.5% open. A cold re-engagement needs a genuine NEW-value news angle (per the brief) and careful warm-up, not a rushed this-week send. I'd rather build that properly next cycle than burn deliverability. The two warm, trigger-based campaigns above will outperform it on near-term conversion by a wide margin.
**Recommendation:** Run Proposal 1 (Tuesday) and Proposal 2 (Thursday) this week. Non-overlapping audiences, no fatigue risk.
